answer: An aged coin can back only one key. Each key must bind one coin that has sat on a ridge of 16 unmoved epochs and post a 17 POA bond. Each epoch a gale audits bound coins at random, and the key files a pigment, the signed ownership mark of its coin. The board stores one pigment per coin; a second bind, a coin younger than 16 epochs, or a conflicting pigment burns the 17 POA bond. A farm of 400 keys with one aged coin can file only one pigment, so 399 keys each burn 17 POA: 399 x 17 = 6,783 POA the attacker forfeits.
